# The regulatory ceiling on price-led growth

NLEM 2022 lists **384 medicines across 27 therapeutic categories**, adding 34
and dropping 26 relative to the previous list. Medicines on the list are subject
to ceiling prices fixed by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority once the
Department of Pharmaceuticals incorporates them into the Drug Price Control
Order. Cardiovascular medicines are among the categories covered.

## Why this matters for prioritisation

This signal is the reason the scoring framework weights constant-price and
volume growth above reported value growth, and treats price erosion as a
negative in the competitive-headroom pillar.

In a market where a meaningful share of the essential cardiovascular basket sits
under administered ceiling prices, a strategy built on realising price is
structurally fragile. Growth that is visible in MAT but absent from MAT CP and
QTY MAT is growth that a single revision of the ceiling price can remove.

The practical implication for Cipla: prefer spaces where the volume line and the
constant-price line are both moving, and treat any space where reported growth
substantially exceeds real growth as lower quality, regardless of how attractive
the headline number looks.
